question: Which statement best describes The three states?
options: .then(onFulfilled, onRejected) registers handlers for the settled value. .catch(onRejected) is shorthand for .then(undefined, onRejected) and handles rejections. .finally(fn) runs regardless of outcome (cleanup) and passes the value/reason through unchanged. Each of these returns a NEW promise, which is what enables chaining.

A promise starts pending (the async work hasn't finished). It then settles exactly once, becoming either fulfilled (resolved with a value) or rejected (failed with a reason). Once settled, a promise is immutable — its state and value never change again, which makes promises safe to pass around and attach handlers to even after they've settled.

Promise.all(arr) waits for all to fulfill (or rejects on the first rejection) and returns an array of values. Promise.allSettled(arr) waits for all to settle and returns {status, value/reason} for each, never rejecting. Promise.race(arr) settles as soon as the FIRST promise settles (fulfilled or rejected). Promise.any(arr) fulfills with the first FULFILLMENT, rejecting only if all reject (with an AggregateError).

Because every .then returns a new promise, you can chain steps top-to-bottom. Whatever a .then callback returns becomes the fulfillment value of the next .then. Crucially, if a callback returns a promise, the chain WAITS for it to settle and unwraps its value before continuing — this is how you sequence dependent async steps without nesting.

Once settled, a promise is immutable — its state and value never change again, which makes promises safe to pass around and attach handlers to even after they've settled.

question: Which statement best describes then / catch / finally?
options: Promise.all(arr) waits for all to fulfill (or rejects on the first rejection) and returns an array of values. Promise.any(arr) fulfills with the first FULFILLMENT, rejecting only if all reject (with an AggregateError).

A rejection (or a thrown error inside a .then callback) skips all subsequent .then handlers and jumps to the next .catch in the chain — like throw/catch but for async. One .catch at the end can therefore handle errors from any earlier step. After a .catch handles the error, the chain returns to the fulfilled track unless the handler re-throws.

question: Which statement best describes Chaining and value transformation?
options: new Promise((resolve, reject) => { ... }) wraps a callback-based or timed operation. The executor runs synchronously; you call resolve(value) on success or reject(reason) on failure. Promise.resolve(v) and Promise.reject(e) create already-settled promises. This is how you 'promisify' legacy callback APIs.

Promise.resolve(v) and Promise.reject(e) create already-settled promises. This is how you 'promisify' legacy callback APIs.

Promise reaction callbacks (.then/.catch/.finally) always run as MICROTASKS — on the same tick, after the current synchronous code finishes but before any setTimeout/macrotask. So even a Promise.resolve().then(...) runs after all sync code, yet before a setTimeout(0) scheduled earlier. This ordering is a frequent interview question.
